labels.quote: Finding Fault: Detecting Issues in a Versioned Ontology

Abstract. Understanding ontology evolution is becoming an active topic of in-
terest for ontology engineers, e.g., there exist large collaboratively-developed on-
tologies but, unlike in software engineering, comparatively little is understood
about the dynamics of historical changes, especially at a fine level of granularity.
Only recently has there been a systematic analysis of changes across ontology
versions, but still at a coarse-grained level. The National Cancer Institute (NCI)
Thesaurus (NCIt) is a large, collaboratively-developed ontology, used for various
Web and research-related purposes, e.g., as a medical research controlled vocab-
ulary. The NCI has published ten years worth of monthly versions of the NCIt
as Web Ontology Language (OWL) documents, and has also published reports
on the content of, development methodology for, and applications of the NCIt.
In this paper, we carry out a fine-grained analysis of asserted axiom dynamics
throughout the evolution of the NCIt from 2003 to 2012. From this, we are able
to identify axiomatic editing patterns that suggest significant regression editing
events in the development history of the NCIt.
